data.title: Software giant SAP weighs major job cuts as AI transforms sector, sources say
data.description: FRANKFURT, Nov 27 : German business software maker SAP , Germany's most valuable company, is preparing to cut a sizeable number of jobs, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Friday. News about the potential job cuts comes as enterprise software makers, including SAP, grapple with the expansion of artificial intelligence. SAP's software runs accounting and payroll at many of the world's biggest firms. The works council of SAP, which employs around 113,000 staff worldwide, has not yet been informed about the plans, one of the people said. Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday that SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-driven restructuring, citing people familiar with the matter. CEO Christian Klein and Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam indicated at investor events in recent weeks that a reduction of the group's workforce was on the cards. SAP, which has a market capitalisation of €238.5 billion ($261.9 billion), is seeking to integrate AI into its products under a strategic push by its CEO. The firm, which trimmed its outlook in July as AI-focused deals weighed on its earnings, said in early 2024 that it would review 8,000 jobs, but cutbacks in slow-growing businesses have since been offset by new hires in more dynamic areas. Recent moves have pointed to a more cost-conscious approach. An SAP executive told Reuters last month the company was replacing some expensive AI models powering its products with cheaper alternatives. ($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: UK pensions minister says no evidence personal data comprised in cyber incident
data.description: LONDON, Nov 27 : Work and pensions minister Pat McFadden said on Friday there is no evidence so far that any personal details were compromised in a cyber incident which prompted his department to take some services offline. Asked whether the incident was a malicious act, McFadden said it was a "serous cyber incident", adding the investigation is ongoing.

data.title: Exclusive-India's election body website flaw exposing voter data fixed after Reuters findings
data.description: MUMBAI, Nov 27 : A security flaw in India's Election Commission (ECI) website that was allowing access to sensitive personal details and documents of some voters has been fixed, after Reuters discovered the vulnerability and alerted the institution. Researchers said the flaw, which Reuters is the first to report, could have been easily abused. The security issue, and the fix, come months ahead of elections in key Indian states, including the most populous, Uttar Pradesh, and while the ECI is facing growing public anger over a contentious drive to update voter lists. Opposition parties and activists have said the drive has disenfranchised millions of voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party. The ECI says it has complied with all regulations, while the BJP argues opposition groups are misleading the country after failing to win elections. A Reuters review over more than a month of the ECI's website showed that when a voter logged into their account and requested a telephone call with their local electoral officer, the network tab in an ordinary browser's developer tools, opened with a simple right click, started showing the reference number of the form submitted online to enrol as voters or update their information. On using those reference numbers to book the call, the same network details started revealing personal information such as the name, phone number, email, date of birth and address of the user, and even file paths to identification documents like passports that were submitted. Such details were not otherwise visible on the browser's main screen, which pointed to a vulnerability in the website's code, said Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who reviewed the Reuters findings step by step on the ECI website. The bigger concern, researchers said, was the reference numbers followed a predictable pattern, meaning hackers could guess them, and automate downloads of large amounts of data. A lay user is unlikely to follow such steps while requesting a call, but cybercriminals could, and also automate the steps to harvest data in bulk and abuse it, they said. Reuters first shared its findings and sought comment from the ECI and its three commissioners on October 26, but they did not respond despite repeated requests. On Thursday, an ECI spokesman said the commission's information technology division had been asked to look into the findings. Hours later, the vulnerability was fixed, with sensitive fields, including personal details and file paths, redacted, according to a Reuters review and the two researchers. The security researchers confirmed the fix effectively blocked any abuse of the data. 'NO SYSTEM COMPLETELY SECURE' Reuters could not determine whether the flaw had been exploited or how long it had existed or how many voters could have been affected. The call-booking feature, in which Reuters detected the security flaw, was introduced in June 2025. It was also not known if any hacker had harvested the data or abused it. India has around 1 billion voters and any of them can log in to the ECI website using their voter ID or mobile numbers. The BJP did not respond to a request for comment. Pawan Khera, a spokesperson for the Congress, the main opposition party, told Reuters on Thursday that the findings were "deeply alarming". "In the context of elections, the exposure of voters' personal information can facilitate targeted intimidation, profiling, voter suppression and the manipulation of vulnerable communities," he said. Told about the findings, former Indian election commissioner Ashok Lavasa said the flaw appeared to be inadvertent, saying "You don’t collect all this information so that you can put it in the public domain." The privacy policy on the ECI's website says while “reasonable efforts” are made to protect the data, “no system can be guaranteed to be completely secure”. The ECI has previously faced scrutiny over how it manages its digital platform. The Hindu newspaper reported in October that an audit by a civic-tech group found access to certain voter details could be switched on or off centrally for state election officials. In 2019, security researcher Saini found ECI's online voter search portal was exposing some voters' personal details via the browser's network tab, a flaw that was fixed following media reporting on it. DOCUMENTS OF REPORTER In the flaw that Reuters found, the browser's network tab, opened by a simple right click to access the form reference number, also revealed file paths of documents uploaded by the voter. Given the predictable pattern the form numbers followed, the security researchers said cybercriminals could have downloaded personal identification documents like passports or national identity cards using simple web-based tools freely available online that required only basic coding knowledge. A Reuters reporter was able to download a copy of his national identification card using the steps. The researchers said cybercriminals could go a step further, using the pattern of numbers to download documents of other voters. "The knowledge of how a browser generally requests documents from the server, combined with disclosed file paths, could have allowed a criminal to download these documents," Saini said. “The server only appeared to check whether a user is logged in, not whether they’re authorised to see a particular document," he added. Ahmed said he found it shocking that such a “basic vulnerability” existed. “I don’t know how they did not adapt to even basic security standards after so many developments in artificial intelligence and technology,” he said. (Editing by Aditya Kalra and Raju Gopalakrishnan)

data.title: Russian AI model fills void in unfinished Gogol novel. Not everyone is happy
data.description: MOSCOW, Nov 27 : Unable to complete his novel "Dead Souls", the writer Nikolai Gogol suffered a breakdown and threw part of his manuscript into the fire only days before he died in 1852. The book - though still regarded as a masterpiece of Russian literature - remained unfinished, with only one of three intended volumes surviving intact. Now a Russian AI model has created its own version of the second volume that Gogol burnt, in a bold experiment to test whether artificial intelligence can capture the spirit and style of a great author. The new book, "Dead Souls: Revival", has caught the imagination of some readers while leaving critics cold. Linguists, engineers and historians were all involved in the project by GigaChat, an AI model developed by banking and tech conglomerate Sber. The person in charge, Vladislav Otroshenko, said it had taken about four months for the machine to develop a plausible literary style. "It handled the artistic side of the task, and the plot element in particular, very well," he told Reuters. "It is a bestseller ... Readers are genuinely interested in it. Does it have artistic value? Of course it does, because it is the first unique, unprecedented experiment of its kind. And we were working with the most challenging style in Russian literature, Gogol's style and poetics." MASTER OF SATIRE AND DARK COMEDY Born in what is now Ukraine, then part of the Russian empire, Gogol wrote his major works in Russian. He is claimed by both countries as a huge literary figure, known especially for his satire and dark comedy. In the first, surviving, part of "Dead Souls", he created a rogue's gallery of characters led by the swindler Chichikov, who concocts a financial scam based on "acquiring" dead serf peasants still registered as belonging to their landlords. But Gogol, tortured by creative and spiritual doubts, was unable to complete the second and third parts of the book in which he had intended to portray the moral regeneration of the protagonist. Igor, a Muscovite who attended the GigaChat book launch, said it really felt true to the spirit of the original. "The book is truly unique, and I believe that admirers of Gogol now have an opportunity to assess it, compare it and see how Chichikov's adventures ended," he enthused. But Larisa, a visitor to the Gogol Museum in Moscow, said there was no way for AI to successfully capture what was lost. "It will not move me and I don't even want to read it," she said. Gogol expert Artyom Nikitin said that by the same logic, AI could write sequels to any number of works. "But I believe that a literary work does not automatically flow from everything that an author created before," he said. "Even if we know the author's language, style and plot lines, that does not point us to what they will write next."

data.title: Explainer-Black Friday test for retailers as tight budgets meet AI-savvy shoppers
data.description: Nov 27 : Black Friday has evolved from a one-day frenzy of pre-dawn store crowds to weeks of online and in-store promotions, with retailers including Walmart and Target vying for more than $1 trillion in expected US holiday spending this year. But stretched budgets loom over the traditional kick-off to the holiday shopping season, as inflation rises and shoppers increasingly turn to AI to find the best deals and the lowest prices.  WHY IS IT CALLED 'BLACK' FRIDAY? In the early 1960s, police officers in Philadelphia described the chaos from suburban tourists descending on the city's stores the day after Thanksgiving as "Black Friday." The phrase did not describe a positive boost in retail sales until the late 1980s, when merchants spread the narrative of being "in the red" until massive Black Friday sales allowed them to turn a profit, or put them "in the black." HOW MUCH ARE SHOPPERS EXPECTED TO SPEND? The National Retail Federation expects US sales in November and December 2026 to rise 4.2 per cent year-on-year to $1.013 trillion, higher than the 3.1 per cent growth recorded a year earlier. Part of the estimated increase, however, is due to inflation. The latest Labor Department's Consumer Price Index report showed a strong buildup of underlying inflation pressures for the third straight month in October, amid rising costs for food and accommodation and oil price hikes due to the US-Israel war against Iran. The trade body estimates 182.7 million consumers will shop over the Thanksgiving weekend, down from 202.9 million last year. Several retailers, including Walmart, Ross Stores, Gap, Bath & Body Works and Lowe's, have also issued cautious holiday season forecasts citing uneven demand from selective consumers. A Deloitte survey showed spending during the Black Friday to Cyber Monday period is expected to remain unchanged from a year earlier at $624 per shopper, although participation was seen reaching a 10-year high of 87 per cent.  WHEN DO BLACK FRIDAY SALES START? Black Friday has increasingly become a weeks-long promotional period, with October events such as Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days and Target's Circle Week now kicking off holiday shopping. More than half of consumers surveyed by Deloitte had already purchased holiday gifts during the October promotions. Meanwhile, retailer Costco kicked off holiday promotions on October 30 and rolled out another round of deals on November 16, which are set to run until the end of the month. Walmart's "Deals & More" event started on November 12 and will run through December 2. Amazon and Best Buy launched Black Friday sales on November 19, with promotions running through November 30 and November 28, respectively. HOW ARE SHOPPERS FINDING DEALS? Consumers are increasingly using AI to compare prices, research products and scout for deals, with nearly one in five beginning their shopping with AI tools, according to Salesforce. AI and digital agents are expected to influence $75.8 billion, or 21 per cent, of global Cyber Week sales this year, the company added. Price comparisons and product recommendations are among the most common uses. Salesforce also said AI-driven traffic to retailers' websites has more than doubled from a year earlier, with shoppers arriving through AI referrals twice as likely to make purchases than typical e-commerce shoppers. WHAT DEALS ARE RETAILERS OFFERING? Electronics remains among the most heavily promoted categories. A Reuters review of retailers' websites found Walmart was offering an 85-inch Vizio Quantum TV for $498, down from $698, while Best Buy had cut prices for a 65-inch TCL TV to $229.99 from $469.99 and HP laptops to $449.99 from $799.99. Apple was offering gift cards worth up to $300 during Cyber Weekend, which spans Black Friday to Cyber Monday. Toy cars and racing vehicles such as Hot Wheels, LEGO sets and Barbie dolls, were among the leading gift picks in the toy category, an NRF survey showed last week. Retailers are also promoting beauty products, home goods and appliances, including a Blackstone grill at Walmart for $150, down from $224, and discounts by Ulta Beauty on brands including Sol de Janeiro, Tarte, MAC and Morphe.

data.title: Exclusive-Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 27 : Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen. In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities." A ONE-STOP SHOP Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force's IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.  Among them are the Air Force's Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 US Air Force locations around the world. SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. Cloud One is among the US military's biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.  "A breach here is a big deal," one of the sources said. Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said.  Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment. A RANGE OF DISRUPTION The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused.  Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked. All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity. One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case. Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers. STRING OF HACKS News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas.  The US government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department. Cloud One has long been in the crosshairs of hackers. In a 2023 commentary carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One's leadership touted what they called a "100 per cent success rate" in beating back what they said was a "staggering" number of attempts to penetrate the platform. "There is no room for error when it comes to security," Cloud One's leadership wrote.

data.title: Exclusive-Volkswagen drags rivals Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 billion India tax fight
data.description: NEW DELHI, Nov 27 : Volkswagen has told an Indian court that tax authorities have wrongly singled it out over how it imports car parts at lower tariffs, alleging rivals Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia do the same, its latest salvo as it seeks to quash a $1.2 billion tax demand. The German carmaker has been fighting since 2025 to quash the record tax demand over allegations it "deliberately" imported components at a 10 per cent tariff and then assembled them into complete cars in India, evading the higher tariffs of around 30 per cent applicable on car kits. Volkswagen has denied the allegations, describing the case as a matter of "life and death" that could "wipe out" all of its investments in India, where it has just a 2 per cent market share. The dispute coincides with the German carmaker's challenges back home due to worker disputes over pay, and falling sales in its key Chinese market. After India accused VW of being the only carmaker indulging in such practices, the German company's unit in a non-public Mumbai court filing dated November 10 said "every manufacturer of comparable cars" follows the same "parts/components model" and pays duty at 10 per cent. If VW succeeds with its arguments about how its rivals import car parts, other carmakers could potentially face heightened scrutiny in the world's third-largest auto market. TAX DEMAND 'DESERVES TO BE QUASHED' "The contention that all other manufacturers paid duty at 30 per cent while the petitioner alone paid 10 per cent is unfortunate and factually incorrect," Volkswagen's India unit said in the filing, seen by Reuters, and being reported for the first time. The tax demand "deserves to be quashed for requiring the petitioner alone to pay 30 per cent duty while all other manufacturers pay 10 per cent," it added. To support its argument, VW attached a one-page table showing import shipment numbers of Mercedes, BMW, Hyundai's sister company Kia, Isuzu Motors and SAIC Motor's India unit JSW MG Motor, the filing showed. VW's India unit, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, declined to comment citing ongoing legal proceedings. Kia declined to comment on Volkswagen's submission, but said it imports car components in accordance with applicable laws. The other rival carmakers it cited in the filing did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did India's tax authorities. In an October submission to the court, seen by Reuters, Indian tax authorities described VW's conduct as one of "fraud and subterfuge". TARIFF DISPUTES LONG A SORE POINT FOR FOREIGN INVESTORS Tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, as investigations and lawsuits can drag on for years, triggering business uncertainty. Global liquor majors currently are sparring with New Delhi over the tariff rate on bulk Scotch imports, though Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law of the land. In the VW dispute, India has alleged the carmaker shipped nearly complete Audi, Skoda and Volkswagen cars to its India plant but as individual parts and in separate consignments to avoid paying higher taxes applicable on car kits, and used internal software to manage such imports. After VW initiated a court challenge months after receiving a tax demand in 2024, Indian authorities told the Mumbai judge that other carmakers were paying rightful duty on their parts imports. VW SAYS IT IS BEING WRONGLY SINGLED OUT VW is disputing that argument with its own analysis, its latest court filing showed. BMW had 390,360 "major import shipments" of car components in 2024, while Mercedes had 80,972, all imported under the lower tariff rate category, VW said in its submission, without elaborating. VW is of the view that such a high number of component imports by rivals are also then used to assemble cars, just like it does, and so the carmaker is being wrongly singled out by New Delhi, according to two people familiar with the matter. However, a third person familiar with the dispute said for VW to succeed in its arguments, it will have to show that its rivals' imports were used to assemble complete vehicles. The court in Mumbai will on Monday decide on Volkswagen's challenge, but the people familiar with the matter said it is likely the court will for now only rule on whether tax authorities could have gone back 12 years in scrutinising VW imports or not.

data.title: 2026 in photos: AI, robots and new technology
data.description: Nov 27 : Technology advanced rapidly this year and long-anticipated developments in artificial intelligence, drones and robots appeared to be materializing, fast.  AI now permeates almost every aspect of life, from fashion and food to counseling and education, for good and for bad. In schools, for instance, teachers are having to rethink how they teach and test in a world of smart chatbots available to all. But AI-enabled technology can also allow medical students to train with virtual simulations, or help children who are hard of hearing understand science lessons. Illustrating technology through photography is not always easy. While robots certainly can be eye-catching — particularly when paired with humans in unexpected ways — concepts like AI or cybercrime often need a creative touch. Sometimes that might be through a glimpse into the world of the billionaire executives who run the big tech firms. Or it might be by documenting the backlash to the water-thirsty data centers springing up to power the AI boom, or by photographing in the bunkers of Ukraine where drones are transforming warfare. And sometimes, it just means taking really cool robot pictures.  (Writing by Rosalba O'Brien; Editing by Alexandra Hudson)

data.title: Oil on track to snap three-week losing streak over supply fears
data.description: LONDON, Nov 27 : Oil prices were on track to snap a three-week losing streak on Friday, riding four sessions of gains, as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure fanned concern over Middle East supplies. Brent crude futures rose 73 cents, or 0.8 per cent, to $97.30 a barrel by 0935 GMT, after hitting their highest since November 9 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures at $85.85 a barrel, were up $2.17, or 2.6 per cent, from Wednesday's close. There was no Thursday settlement for WTI because of the US Thanksgiving holiday. "We think Brent can still push above $100 a barrel without another major escalation in the Middle East, but that increasingly requires evidence of constrained deliverable supply," ANZ analysts Brian Martin and Daniel Hynes said in a research note. Prices have slipped in recent weeks as investors were relieved that US President Donald Trump did not step up military action on Iran after the midterm elections. However, Iran has continued to attack ships transiting the key waterway of the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting oil exports, while Yemeni Houthis have struck Saudi Arabian infrastructure. "(The) price in the Bay of Oman currently seems to signal that there is ample supply of crude oil available. But assuming that this is a stable status quo is probably a faulty assumption," said SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop. "Add in that the Houthis and what they do to Saudi Arabia and their semi-control of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, and you may not want to sit short oil, to put it mildly." Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck it on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said. The strike was the latest blow to key Saudi facilities, a day after the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery and a major crude export hub. OPEC+, which includes Saudi Arabia and Russia, had an agreement in principle to maintain oil output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at a meeting on Sunday, three people with knowledge of the talks said. Ukraine has intensified drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since the end of October, with the latest incident causing a fire at the Slavyansk ECO refinery in Russia's southern region of Krasnodar.  Separately, fires disrupted activity at Thailand's Bangchak refinery and Venezuela's Amuay refinery on Thursday. (Additional reporting by Florence Tan and Sudarshan Varadhan; Editing by Kate Mayberry, DJ Yap and Clarence Fernandez)

data.title: Better fare transparency, support for ComfortDelGro’s taxi, private-hire drivers from Dec 1
data.description: SINGAPORE: Drivers on ComfortDelGro's Zig platform will have more transparency in their earnings and better support in cases of suspension or serious injury from Dec 1. This comes after Zig became the first platform operator to sign collective agreements with the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) and National Taxi Association (NTA) on Friday (Nov 27). The NPHVA and NTA are both affiliated with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and have legal powers to represent private-hire and taxi drivers under the Platform Workers Act that came into effect in January 2025. NTUC secretary-general Ng Chee Meng called these first collective agreements with Zig a "significant milestone". "They bring real outcomes for drivers, with greater transparency of their earnings, formal consultation before major changes are made to their work, and clearer channels to raise and resolve concerns," he said. He added that Zig had set an example for the sector by being the first to go further than recognising Singapore's platform work associations to sign collective agreements with them. "We thank ComfortDelGro for its partnership and call on other platform operators to do the same for their drivers too," said Mr Ng.Other major platform operators in Singapore include Grab, Gojek, TADA and Trans-Cab's Smile. Advance figures by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) released on Friday estimated that there are 57,000 to 59,100 private-hire car drivers and taxi drivers who did this as their regular form of employment in 2026. TRANSPARENT FARES The collective agreements represent an understanding between Zig and the associations on the terms and conditions of work for the represented workers. One outcome is to formalise Zig's existing practice of giving drivers a clear, itemised statement for every trip and payout. The statement shows what each fare is made up of, including surcharges and incentives, commission, payment processing fees, Central Provident Fund contributions and net earnings. "This allows drivers to check their take-home earnings for each trip and better track their overall earnings," NPHVA, NTA and Zig said in a joint statement. "They can then plan their hours, so they do not stay on the road longer than needed and can take regular breaks to look after their health." A minimum fare of S$9 (US$7) also applies to ComfortRide trips on Zig, which may be reviewed as operating costs and market conditions evolve, they added.SUSPENSIONS The agreements will also provide clearer recourse and support for drivers on Zig, said the joint statement. NPHVA and NTA members can raise grievances through the associations and escalate them to Zig's management. "For example, except in serious cases, Zig will warn or notify drivers before suspending or removing them from the platform, and members can appeal through their association and receive a written outcome with reasons," said NPHVA, NTA and Zig. "If a dispute remains unresolved, either party will be able to engage the Ministry of Manpower for conciliation and, if needed, the Industrial Arbitration Court." Serious cases refer to gross or serious misconduct, or where regulations require immediate action. The driver may be suspended while Zig investigates such cases. SERIOUS INJURIES Support extends to work-related injuries and other benefits. Drivers who hire Zig vehicles are already covered by benefits such as a personal accident scheme and rental incentives. From Dec 1, Zig will help eligible drivers apply for government-paid leave, including maternity, paternity, shared parental and childcare leave. Another benefit for Zig drivers will be access to health screening at preferential rates. These benefits, alongside other support measures, will also be made available to eligible private-hire vehicle drivers, said NPHVA, NTA and Zig. This includes drivers who do not rent Zig vehicles but take Zig jobs, and who are members of NPHVA and NTA. NPHVA is also separately in discussions with ComfortDelGro Rent-A-Car on more support for private-hire drivers who rent its vehicles. Extra support is also available for eligible drivers who are permanently incapacitated in an accident while doing platform work, and who qualify for work injury compensation. They will receive up to S$2,000 as interim relief on top of the compensation required by law. DATA-SHARING Zig also became the first platform operator to commit, in a collective agreement, to share data on drivers' work with the platform work associations. The business will share aggregated figures on earnings, online hours and completed trips with NPHVA and NTA. It will also provide "further information to verify drivers' earnings, monitor job trends and handle grievances", the associations and Zig said. Formalising such data-sharing gives the platform work associations a "stronger evidence base to identify emerging issues, track changes in drivers' working conditions and work with Zig on targeted improvements", they said in the joint statement. CONSULTATION ON MAJOR CHANGES Zig also committed to consulting NPHVA and NTA ahead of major work changes that affect drivers' earnings, allowances, deductions or working conditions, except in "urgent cases". It will also provide at least two weeks' notice of adjustments to fares, the app or pilot programmes. "In turn, the platform work associations will bring feedback from drivers on the ground, such as on job availability, operating costs and road safety, so that Zig can take it into account in its business decisions," said the associations and business. They added that drivers who rent from Zig are entitled to preferential commission rates. Zig was the first platform operator to formally recognise the NPHVA and NTA in February 2025. On Friday, ComfortDelGro managing director and group CEO Cheng Siak Kian said: "A strong point-to-point industry depends on the people who keep it moving. "As we transform our business, we want the changes we make to create value for our driver partners and the communities we serve."

data.title: UK pensions department hit by 'cyber incident'
data.description: LONDON: The British government department which administers pensions and welfare payments said on Friday (Nov 27) it had identified a "cyber incident" which was affecting its systems, and it was taking some services offline as a precaution. The Department for Work and Pensions said people would still receive their regular benefit and pension payments as normal and added it hoped to reinstate services soon. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimise any disruption," it said in a statement. British companies and institutions have been increasingly hit by aggressive and regular cyber attacks in recent years, with some suffering months of disruption, including the British Library, a blood testing service, the London Underground, Marks & Spencer, the Co-op and Jaguar Land Rover.

data.title: Dollar set for flat week as haven bids counter yields
data.description: Nov 27 : The dollar was heading towards ending the week roughly unchanged as investors weighed the possible drag from lower US Treasury yields against rising safe-haven demand. Concerns about a deeper fall in the stock market would strengthen expectations of a more dovish Federal Reserve, eroding the dollar's yield advantage.  Conversely, the same bout of risk aversion would boost demand for safe-haven assets, including the dollar, offsetting some of the pressure from lower yields. "We expect the Fed to remain hawkish and the US economy resilient, and our multi-asset strategists remain upbeat on US equities and the AI theme," said Daragh Maher, senior forex strategist at HSBC. "The main risk to our view is that renewed market weakness could erode rate support, with no guarantee that safe-haven demand would again compensate," he said, adding that December’s Fed rate forecasts would be pivotal to the bullish cyclical greenback story. The dollar index started its rally in early November and hit a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier this week. It was last little changed at 103.76 and was on track for a weekly rise of about 0.02 per cent. US stock futures surged on Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares, following a seesawing of AI stocks this week as investors weighed more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology. "The high-beta Australian dollar, Kiwi dollar and Norwegian krone are leading gains in G10, although the moves remain modest compared with their recent losses," Francesco Pesole, forex strategist at ING, said. "That suggests the forward-looking forex market remains cautious about calling an all-clear on risk sentiment," he added. A so-called high-beta currency tends to amplify shifts in global sentiment, outperforming when risk appetite improves and underperforming when it fades. The Norwegian crown rose 0.67 per cent to 9.70 versus the greenback. The Aussie dollar added 0.58 per cent to $0.667, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday. The New Zealand dollar was also supported by results of the general election, which reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner. New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to keep his ruling centre-right coalition in power after official results showed he fell just short of a parliamentary majority. Geopolitics remained in the background but oil prices were on track to snap a three-week losing streak following attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure. Higher Brent crude futures often underpin the dollar against the euro and yen, as they boost revenues for US energy exporters while increasing import costs for the euro zone and Japan. The euro was roughly unchanged at $1.0971 with investors showing little reaction to news that Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos was set to be nominated as the head of the European Central Bank. DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention. Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month. "Broad dollar strength and relative rates favour yen weakness, but the threat of forex intervention limits the yen’s downside, without making 160 an official ceiling," HSBC's Maher argued. "We expect the dollar/yen to trade within 156-160, mostly towards the upper end."

data.title: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description: SHANGHAI: China's share benchmarks jumped 4 per cent and the yuan rose on Friday (Nov 27), after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market . Chinese stocks have struggled this year despite policy easing, reflecting investor concerns over weak domestic demand, a prolonged property downturn and uncertainty over the economic outlook hurt by trade wars and geopolitics. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended 4.2 per cent up and the blue-chip CSI300 index was 3.7 per cent higher at the close, both notching their biggest daily gains since October 2024 when China rolled out massive stimulus measures to revive the market. China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 15 per cent, the biggest one-day jump in two years. The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 1.9 per cent while the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 6 per cent. In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the Cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy", state media Xinhua reported. The Cabinet added that Central Huijin - the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp - would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity. The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets. "It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong. "Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."The Chinese yuan gained 0.1 per cent against the dollar in offshore trading, reversing earlier weakness to hit its strongest in three weeks. The currency is nearing its firmest level in four years. "It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package," said Jason Chan, a Hong Kong-based strategest at Bank of East Asia. Given the current low investor expectations, any incremental supportive policies would help boost confidence, said Meng Lei, China equity strategist at UBS Securities. The latest statement follows the margin lending relaxation and trading fee reductions announced over the weekend, underscoring the government's growing determination to stabilise markets. LSEG data showed trading volume surged across broad-based benchmarks and sub-indices after the midday break, pointing to a sharp improvement in investor sentiment. The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index and the STAR Chip Index both shot up more than 17 per cent. Indices tracking China's AI, cloud computing and consumer electronics stocks jumped more than 10 per cent. But some analysts said it was too early to suggest the market was near a bottom as support from the national team alone was unlikely to lead to a sustained rally. "There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank. "I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals... A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom." Also on Friday, Xinhua Finance reported that regulators will launch a campaign to further tighten rules on share sales by controlling shareholders of listed companies. Regulators will also guard against listings by "pseudo-tech" companies, or firms that inflate earnings, the state media said.
